pitch_detail.notes: 70m; begins in the blocky line of face holds just left of the gully/chimney on the left edge of the buttress, wide crack near the end, mostly low 5th class
20m; low-angle snow/rock climbing to a corner
30m; corner climbing with some fixed protection to a ledge
40m; flakes and cracks to a pedestal
30m; hidden corner climbing
45m; long seam/finger-crack system
30m; featured arete with a shallow dihedral
Follow the left side of the buttress to the top; moderate climbing to the summit ridge (total route length 1,400 ft / 14 pitches)
Excellent finger locks and jamming on a spectacular pitch; avoid the easier-looking chimney around the corner to the right — it's off-route.
Bolted face climbing on fragile-feeling flakes; a standout ('money') pitch.
Crux pitch on quality rock ('money pitch').
A rising traverse under a green roof with a chimney and 5.9+ offwidth section; rock gets looser and harder to protect toward the end. Often combined with P9-P10 into long (~60m) leads.
High-quality 'money pitch' climbing; often combined with P8/P10.
High-quality 'money pitch' climbing; often combined with P8/P9.
Committing moves down low lead into splitter cracks; some parties skip this pitch to save time.
Final pitch to the top of the spire; details not well documented in available trip reports.
Bolted groove to a spacious ledge.
Flake, thin crack, and face moves to a bolted belay.
Right-leaning seam traverse into steep face on desperate friction moves — reported mental crux; offset cams useful.
Knobs and face holds; well-bolted.
Corner climbing finishing with a short bolted layback.
Ramp/corner with sparse gear leading into steep bolted face; manage rope carefully here on the rappel descent.
Sustained friction climbing protected by bolts and small cams.
Steep, juggy face into a flaring corner; crux pitch, can be aided at A0 to avoid the 5.11a free moves.
Low-angle slab, easy but runout; simul-climbable for confident 5.8 climbers
Steeper rock, closer bolt spacing as difficulty increases
Mostly easy but the most runout section; fair rock quality; P15-17 hard to protect
Hardest climbing, sport-bolted; both 5.10 pitches well protected
Face and moss slab climbing to tree belay
Bolted climbing with run-out section near top
Trad climbing with poor crack quality; tricky protection
Gear and bolted climbing; anchors can be hard to find
Difficult protection; finger crack section; harder than grade suggests
Sporty climbing; sparse bolts; exposed slab
The Jenga Traverse—knife-edge crossing with loose blocks and minimal protection; the crux of the route; 5.5 climbing but PG protection makes it feel harder
Bolts to chains, then trends left past additional anchor sets.
Corner pitch with traditional gear leading into a slab section.
Bolts with small trad gear, trending up-right through corners and over a roof to the anchor.
Easier, slabbier climbing to the top of the cliff.
Climbs a short face to clean ramps, ending at a ledge belay.
Traverses across a saddle to a chain anchor.
Bolted climbing to a semi-hanging belay on a small ledge; significant exposure. Can be combined with P4 using alpine draws.
Finishes up an arete/basalt band to the summit.

pitch_detail.grade: 5.8 published / felt closer to 5.10 to a 2013 party
pitch_detail.notes: Broken, loose crack pitch
Aesthetic chimney with minimal protection; a large offset/Big Bro-style cam is useful
Very loose terrain; simul-climb from a false summit to the true summit
